project.prompt: Design a housing for my board (g.zip).

product.name: Bluetooth speaker main board (g.zip) with two-piece screw-together housing
product.summary: The board is most likely the main board of a small battery-powered Bluetooth speaker or hands-free audio receiver. The supplied data names a Bluetooth audio SoC module, a class-D stereo amplifier, a Li-ion charger fed from USB-C, a 3.3 V regulator, a MEMS microphone, a status LED and a connector to a separate key board. Confidence is fairly high on that function because the values come from the board data; the picture shows only pads and silkscreen outlines with no legible markings, so exact part numbers, the battery and speaker connection points and the identity of the unnamed two-pad parts remain open. The housing is a 112 x 41 x 18 mm tray and lid with 2 mm walls, split at the board top surface and closed by four self-tapping screws in corner bosses outside the board outline; the board has no mounting holes, so it rests on floor ribs and is clamped by lid posts. Scale reference: the s
product.powerInput: USB-C, 5 V, about 1 A assumed for charging; a single Li-ion cell (3.0 to 4.2 V) presumably connects off-board

parts.name: Bottom shell (tray)
parts.function: Carries the board on floor ribs, locates its edges and takes the four screws from below.
parts.material: ABS or PC+ABS (PLA/PETG for a printed prototype)
parts.process: Injection moulding, straight pull, 1 to 2 degrees draft; or FDM print open face up
parts.evidence: Designed for this board: 2 mm walls; 1.5 mm clearance at front and rear, 6 mm at each end to make room for corner screw pillars because the board has no mounting holes. Rim is level with the board top surface (z = -2.9) so every edge opening is a simple notch in the lid.
parts.unknowns: Add a tongue-and-groove lip to the rim and counterbored screw pillars at the four corners in CAD. If the microphone turns out to be bottom-ported, add a 1 mm sound hole and gasket in the floor under it.

parts.name: Top shell (lid)
parts.function: Covers the components, clamps the board with posts and carries the screw bosses and all openings.
parts.material: ABS or PC+ABS (PLA/PETG for a printed prototype)
parts.process: Injection moulding, straight pull with rim notches as shut-offs; or FDM print roof down
parts.evidence: Designed for this board: inner ceiling at z = 7, which is 1.9 mm above the tallest part (the round part P4, estimated 8 mm). Openings: USB-C notch about 13 x 7 mm in the rear wall at x = +40 (large enough for the plug overmould, because the receptacle mouth sits 3.5 mm behind the outer face); harness notch about 8 x 2.5 mm in the rear wall at x = -40 for the key board cable; 2.6 mm hole in the roo
parts.unknowns: Lid height depends on the real height of P4. If the key board mounts in the lid, its outline and button positions are needed to add button holes.

parts.name: Board support ribs (moulded into bottom shell)
parts.function: Hold the board 2.5 mm above the floor so through-hole leads clear it.
parts.process: Integral with the bottom shell moulding
parts.evidence: No mounting holes were found, so the board is carried on ribs. Rib positions avoid the through-hole pads of P4 at x = 22.
parts.unknowns: Add short edge-locating ribs at the board ends and sides in CAD, 0.2 mm clear of the outline. Check the bottom copper for anything the ribs would touch.

parts.name: Board hold-down posts (moulded into top shell)
parts.function: Press on empty areas of the board so it is clamped against the ribs when the lid is screwed down.
parts.process: Integral with the top shell moulding; leave 0.1 to 0.2 mm crush or add a foam pad
parts.evidence: Positions chosen in component-free areas of the picture: board coordinates about (40, 8), (42, 30), (80, 8) and (3, 16).
parts.unknowns: Confirm there are no tracks needing clearance or tall hand-fitted parts at these four spots.

parts.name: Housing screw, 2.6 x 12 mm self-tapping pan head
parts.function: Clamp the bottom shell to the bosses in the top shell.
parts.evidence: Design choice: the board has no holes, so the screws sit outside the board outline in the 6 mm end margins.

parts.name: Status LED light pipe
parts.function: Carries light from the status LED up to the roof of the lid.
parts.process: Injection moulding, press fit in the lid; clear printed rod for a prototype
parts.evidence: D1 sits at board (4, 3), about 3 mm inside the front-left corner, so a vertical pipe to the roof is the shortest path.
parts.unknowns: A thinned translucent window in the lid would also work if the LED is bright enough.

parts.name: Microphone acoustic boot
parts.function: Seals the microphone to the 1 mm port in the lid so it hears outside sound and not the speaker cavity.
parts.material: Silicone or TPE, 40 to 50 Shore A
parts.process: Compression or injection moulded boot with a 1.2 mm bore
parts.evidence: MK1 sits at board (92, 4) near the front-right corner; a top-ported microphone needs a sealed path to the housing surface.
parts.unknowns: Check whether the microphone is top- or bottom-ported (look for a hole in the board under it). If bottom-ported, replace this with a 2.5 mm gasket under the board and a port in the floor.

parts.name: Main board
parts.function: Carries the Bluetooth audio, amplifier, charging and regulator circuits.
parts.process: Standard PCB fabrication, single-sided SMT reflow plus one through-hole part
parts.evidence: Outline 96 x 34 mm, 1.6 mm thick, 2 copper layers, taken from the board data; green solder mask and white silkscreen in the picture. No mounting holes.
parts.unknowns: A silkscreen rectangle with no pads at board x 8.8 to 23.2, y 0.9 to 4.1 may be an antenna keep-out or a label area; keep metal away from it until checked.

parts.name: Bluetooth audio SoC module
parts.function: Receives Bluetooth audio, decodes it, reads the keys and microphone and drives the amplifier and LED.
parts.package: 24-pad module, two rows, about 1.3 mm pitch
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 24 pads in two rows of 12, silkscreen outline about 16.3 x 12.4 mm in the picture.
parts.unknowns: No marking is visible. Read the top mark or shield label on the real part, and find which end holds the antenna so the housing keeps it clear of screws.

parts.name: Class-D stereo amplifier
parts.function: Drives the two speakers from the module's line outputs.
candidates: other 5 V stereo class-D in a 14 or 16 pin SOP
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 14-pad outline, 7 pads per side at about 1.5 mm pitch, about 10.3 x 4.4 mm; it covers the pad groups listed as P13, U2, P15, P16, P17, P18, P22 and P23.
parts.unknowns: Exact part and where the four speaker outputs leave the board; read the marking and follow the output pads.

parts.name: Li-ion charger
parts.function: Charges the single lithium cell from USB 5 V.
parts.package: 6-pin dual-row SMD, about 2 mm pad pitch
candidates: Linear single-cell charger in a 6-pin package
TP4056 / MCP73831 / LTC4054-class linear chargers (package to confirm)
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 6-pad outline, 3 pads per side, about 5.3 x 4.4 mm, next to the USB-C connector; it covers the pad groups listed as U3, P10, P24 and P25.
parts.unknowns: Charge current and whether protection is on this board or in the battery pack; read the marking and the programming resistor.

parts.name: 3.3 V regulator
parts.function: Makes the 3.3 V logic rail from the battery rail.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 4-pad outline about 3.4 x 2 mm; it covers the pad groups listed as U5 and P20.
parts.unknowns: Linear or switching; no inductor is clearly paired with it, so an LDO is likely.

parts.name: USB-C receptacle
parts.function: Charging input, 5 V.
candidates: 6-pin power-only USB-C receptacle with shell tabs
16-pin USB 2.0 type if data pins are fitted
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 7 pads; the silkscreen outline about 9.3 x 7.4 mm runs to the rear board edge (board y = 34) in the picture.
parts.unknowns: Whether D+/D- are wired, and how far the shell overhangs the board edge; that sets the size of the wall opening.

parts.name: Key board connector, 5-pin
parts.function: Takes the harness to a separate key (button) board.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 5 pads at about 1.5 mm pitch; outline about 7.3 x 3.8 mm, 2 mm inside the rear board edge at the left.
parts.unknowns: Top or side entry and its real height; the key board itself is not in the data.

parts.name: Round two-pin through-hole part (probably bulk electrolytic capacitor)
parts.function: Probably reservoir capacitance for the amplifier supply.
parts.evidence: Picture shows a 6.6 mm silkscreen circle with two gold through-hole pads about 3.1 mm apart, beside the amplifier. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Could instead be a buzzer or a pair of wire holes for the battery or a speaker. Its height sets the lid height, so measure it; a taller can than 8 mm needs a taller lid.

parts.name: Two-pad part, about 1210 size (capacitor or inductor)
parts.function: Probably bulk decoupling or filtering next to the module.
parts.evidence: Two pads, outline about 3.5 x 2.8 mm at board (30, 20), beside U1. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Identify by look and with an LCR meter.

parts.name: Large two-pad part or wire pads (P6 + P7)
parts.function: Unknown: either a power inductor or fuse in the supply path, or solder pads for battery or speaker wires.
parts.evidence: Two large pads, each 2.5 x 2.16 mm and 6.5 mm apart, inside one silkscreen rectangle about 9.3 x 2.7 mm, just in front of the amplifier. Listed as two single-pad groups.
parts.unknowns: If these are wire pads, the battery or speaker leads leave here and need a route and strain relief in the housing. Check the real board.

parts.name: Two-pad 1206-size part near USB
parts.function: Probably input protection or the charge-current setting part.
parts.evidence: Two pads, outline about 3.4 x 1.5 mm at board (84, 21.5), between the USB-C connector and the charger. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Read its marking or measure it.

parts.name: MEMS microphone
parts.function: Picks up voice for hands-free calls.
parts.package: 4-pad MEMS microphone, about 3.8 x 3 mm class
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 4-pad outline about 4.1 x 3.4 mm in the front-right corner; it covers the pad groups listed as MK1 and P12.
parts.unknowns: Top or bottom port, and analogue or PDM output.

parts.name: Status LED
parts.function: Shows pairing, playing and charging state.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; two pads, 0603-size outline at board (4, 3) in the front-left corner.
parts.unknowns: Colour, and whether it emits upwards or sideways.

connections.label: VBUS
connections.evidence: The charger sits next to the USB-C connector. 1 A is the usual upper limit for small linear chargers and is the peak this path is sized for; not measured.

connections.label: VBAT to amplifier
connections.evidence: Typical for this product class: the amplifier runs straight from the battery rail. Peak estimate for a small stereo class-D on one cell.

connections.label: VBAT reservoir
connections.evidence: The round part sits beside the amplifier, where a bulk capacitor on its supply would be.

connections.label: VBAT to regulator
connections.evidence: A 3.3 V regulator on a single-cell product is fed from the battery rail.

connections.label: 3V3
connections.evidence: The regulator is named 3.3 V and the module is the main 3.3 V load; current is a typical Bluetooth audio peak.

connections.label: 3V3 / mic supply
connections.evidence: MEMS microphones draw under 1 mA; the supply may instead come from a bias pin on the module.

connections.label: Audio L/R
connections.evidence: A Bluetooth audio module feeding a stereo class-D amplifier.

connections.label: Microphone
connections.evidence: The microphone can only serve the audio module; analogue or PDM is not known.

connections.label: Keys
connections.evidence: The connector is named key board connector and sits next to the module.

connections.label: Status LED drive
connections.evidence: The status LED sits beside the module.

connections.label: Light path
connections.evidence: Housing design.

connections.label: Acoustic seal
connections.evidence: Housing design.

connections.label: Four screws into lid bosses
connections.medium: 2.6 mm self-tapping screws plus rim lip
connections.evidence: Housing design.

connections.label: Board rests on ribs
connections.evidence: Housing design; no mounting holes.

connections.label: Board clamped by lid posts
connections.evidence: Housing design; no mounting holes.

unknowns: The board data lists 25 pad groups, but the picture shows they belong to fewer physical parts. I merged them: the amplifier is one 14-pad part, the charger one 6-pad part, the regulator and the microphone one 4-pad part each, and P6 + P7 share one outline.
No battery connector and no speaker connectors were identified. P6/P7 and the round part P4 are the likely candidates for wire pads; check the real board.
This housing encloses the board only. If the battery and speakers must go inside, their sizes are needed and the housing has to grow.
The key board on J3 is not in the data, so no buttons are modelled and the controls list is empty. A harness notch is provided in the rear wall as a placeholder.
Height of P4, estimated at 8 mm, sets the lid height. Measure it.
Microphone port direction (top or bottom) decides whether the sound port goes in the lid or the floor.
Antenna position on the Bluetooth module, and the purpose of the pad-less silkscreen rectangle at the front-left, are unknown. Keep screws and metal parts away from both.
No chip markings are visible; all part numbers are candidate families only.
Bottom-side copper and any bottom-side parts were not shown; the data lists top-side parts only.
All voltages and currents are estimates from typical parts of this class, not measurements.
verifySteps: Measure the tallest part on the assembled board (expected to be P4) and the lead protrusion underneath; adjust lid height and rib height to match.
Photograph the real assembled board top and bottom to read chip markings and to see what P4, P5, P6/P7 and P8 are.
Find where the battery and speaker wires attach and add cable routes or openings for them.
Measure the USB-C shell overhang past the board edge and test a printed rear wall with the intended cable; widen the opening if the plug overmould does not seat.
Check whether there is a hole in the board under the microphone (bottom port) and move the sound port if so.
Get the key board dimensions and button positions, then add its mounts and button holes.
Print the two shells first and check board fit: 0.2 mm edge clearance at the locating ribs, clamp pressure at the four posts, screw engagement in the bosses.
With the board powered, measure VBUS current while charging and the battery-rail current at full volume to confirm the power estimates.
safety: A lithium-ion cell will be connected: do not short or pierce it, use a protected cell, and give it a retained position away from screw tips and sharp ribs.
A linear charger and the class-D amplifier get warm in a sealed plastic box; check temperatures during a full charge and at full volume, especially with a PLA print.
Keep the 12 mm screws within the lid bosses; a longer screw can break through the roof.
Use a flame-rated plastic (UL 94 V-0 PC+ABS) for a production housing that contains a lithium cell.

parts.package: 24-pad module, two rows, about 1.3 mm pitch
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 24 pads in two rows of 12, silkscreen outline about 16.3 x 12.4 mm in the picture.
parts.unknowns: No marking is visible. Read the top mark or shield label on the real part, and find which end holds the antenna so the housing keeps it clear of screws.

parts.name: Class-D stereo amplifier
parts.function: Drives the two speakers from the module's line outputs.
candidates: other 5 V stereo class-D in a 14 or 16 pin SOP
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 14-pad outline, 7 pads per side at about 1.5 mm pitch, about 10.3 x 4.4 mm; it covers the pad groups listed as P13, U2, P15, P16, P17, P18, P22 and P23.
parts.unknowns: Exact part and where the four speaker outputs leave the board; read the marking and follow the output pads.

parts.name: Li-ion charger
parts.function: Charges the single lithium cell from USB 5 V.
parts.package: 6-pin dual-row SMD, about 2 mm pad pitch
candidates: Linear single-cell charger in a 6-pin package
TP4056 / MCP73831 / LTC4054-class linear chargers (package to confirm)
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 6-pad outline, 3 pads per side, about 5.3 x 4.4 mm, next to the USB-C connector; it covers the pad groups listed as U3, P10, P24 and P25.
parts.unknowns: Charge current and whether protection is on this board or in the battery pack; read the marking and the programming resistor.

parts.name: 3.3 V regulator
parts.function: Makes the 3.3 V logic rail from the battery rail.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 4-pad outline about 3.4 x 2 mm; it covers the pad groups listed as U5 and P20.
parts.unknowns: Linear or switching; no inductor is clearly paired with it, so an LDO is likely.

parts.name: USB-C receptacle
parts.function: Charging input, 5 V.
candidates: 6-pin power-only USB-C receptacle with shell tabs
16-pin USB 2.0 type if data pins are fitted
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 7 pads; the silkscreen outline about 9.3 x 7.4 mm runs to the rear board edge (board y = 34) in the picture.
parts.unknowns: Whether D+/D- are wired, and how far the shell overhangs the board edge; that sets the size of the wall opening.

parts.name: Key board connector, 5-pin
parts.function: Takes the harness to a separate key (button) board.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; 5 pads at about 1.5 mm pitch; outline about 7.3 x 3.8 mm, 2 mm inside the rear board edge at the left.
parts.unknowns: Top or side entry and its real height; the key board itself is not in the data.

parts.name: Round two-pin through-hole part (probably bulk electrolytic capacitor)
parts.function: Probably reservoir capacitance for the amplifier supply.
parts.evidence: Picture shows a 6.6 mm silkscreen circle with two gold through-hole pads about 3.1 mm apart, beside the amplifier. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Could instead be a buzzer or a pair of wire holes for the battery or a speaker. Its height sets the lid height, so measure it; a taller can than 8 mm needs a taller lid.

parts.name: Two-pad part, about 1210 size (capacitor or inductor)
parts.function: Probably bulk decoupling or filtering next to the module.
parts.evidence: Two pads, outline about 3.5 x 2.8 mm at board (30, 20), beside U1. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Identify by look and with an LCR meter.

parts.name: Large two-pad part or wire pads (P6 + P7)
parts.function: Unknown: either a power inductor or fuse in the supply path, or solder pads for battery or speaker wires.
parts.evidence: Two large pads, each 2.5 x 2.16 mm and 6.5 mm apart, inside one silkscreen rectangle about 9.3 x 2.7 mm, just in front of the amplifier. Listed as two single-pad groups.
parts.unknowns: If these are wire pads, the battery or speaker leads leave here and need a route and strain relief in the housing. Check the real board.

parts.name: Two-pad 1206-size part near USB
parts.function: Probably input protection or the charge-current setting part.
parts.evidence: Two pads, outline about 3.4 x 1.5 mm at board (84, 21.5), between the USB-C connector and the charger. No value given.
parts.unknowns: Read its marking or measure it.

parts.name: MEMS microphone
parts.function: Picks up voice for hands-free calls.
parts.package: 4-pad MEMS microphone, about 3.8 x 3 mm class
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data. The picture shows one 4-pad outline about 4.1 x 3.4 mm in the front-right corner; it covers the pad groups listed as MK1 and P12.
parts.unknowns: Top or bottom port, and analogue or PDM output.

parts.name: Status LED
parts.function: Shows pairing, playing and charging state.
parts.evidence: Value given in the board data; two pads, 0603-size outline at board (4, 3) in the front-left corner.
parts.unknowns: Colour, and whether it emits upwards or sideways.

unknowns: The board data lists 25 pad groups, but the picture shows they belong to fewer physical parts. I merged them: the amplifier is one 14-pad part, the charger one 6-pad part, the regulator and the microphone one 4-pad part each, and P6 + P7 share one outline.
No battery connector and no speaker connectors were identified. P6/P7 and the round part P4 are the likely candidates for wire pads; check the real board.
This housing encloses the board only. If the battery and speakers must go inside, their sizes are needed and the housing has to grow.
The key board on J3 is not in the data, so no buttons are modelled and the controls list is empty. A harness notch is provided in the rear wall as a placeholder.
Height of P4, estimated at 8 mm, sets the lid height. Measure it.
Microphone port direction (top or bottom) decides whether the sound port goes in the lid or the floor.
Antenna position on the Bluetooth module, and the purpose of the pad-less silkscreen rectangle at the front-left, are unknown. Keep screws and metal parts away from both.
No chip markings are visible; all part numbers are candidate families only.
Bottom-side copper and any bottom-side parts were not shown; the data lists top-side parts only.
All voltages and currents are estimates from typical parts of this class, not measurements.
verifySteps: Measure the tallest part on the assembled board (expected to be P4) and the lead protrusion underneath; adjust lid height and rib height to match.
Photograph the real assembled board top and bottom to read chip markings and to see what P4, P5, P6/P7 and P8 are.
Find where the battery and speaker wires attach and add cable routes or openings for them.
Measure the USB-C shell overhang past the board edge and test a printed rear wall with the intended cable; widen the opening if the plug overmould does not seat.
Check whether there is a hole in the board under the microphone (bottom port) and move the sound port if so.
Get the key board dimensions and button positions, then add its mounts and button holes.
Print the two shells first and check board fit: 0.2 mm edge clearance at the locating ribs, clamp pressure at the four posts, screw engagement in the bosses.
With the board powered, measure VBUS current while charging and the battery-rail current at full volume to confirm the power estimates.
safety: A lithium-ion cell will be connected: do not short or pierce it, use a protected cell, and give it a retained position away from screw tips and sharp ribs.
A linear charger and the class-D amplifier get warm in a sealed plastic box; check temperatures during a full charge and at full volume, especially with a PLA print.
Keep the 12 mm screws within the lid bosses; a longer screw can break through the roof.
Use a flame-rated plastic (UL 94 V-0 PC+ABS) for a production housing that contains a lithium cell.
